title: Coroner's inquest scheduled into RCMP shooting of B.C. mother and son
subtitle: Jovan Christopher Williams, 39, and Shirley Beatrice Williams, 73, were shot and killed by police on April 21, 2016 outside their home in Granisle
article: The B.C. Coroners Service has schedule a public inquest into the deaths of a mother and son who were shot and killed during a confrontation with the RCMP in the tiny B.C. community of Granisle nearly four years ago.

Jovan Christopher Williams, 39, and Shirley Beatrice Williams, 73, were killed April 21, 2016 outside their home in Granisle, a community of about 300 residents about 100 kilometres northwest of Burns Lake.
The RCMP were at the residence after receiving a report of a handgun being drawn during a dispute between neighbours.

A report by Independent Investigations Office of B.C., which investigates into all officer-related incidents that result in serious harm or death, stated that police fired at Jovan Williams after he tossed a molotov cocktail and pointed a rifle at an officer.
The report stated that Shirley Williams was shot after she left the home holding a shotgun and wearing a bulletproof vest.
The IIO investigation concluded with no charges recommended.
Coroner Larry Marzinzik will preside over an inquest into the pair's deaths on June 15 at the Smithers Courthouse.

"The jury will have the opportunity to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances. A jury must not make any finding of legal responsibility or express any conclusion of law," the B.C. Coroners Service said in a release. "An inquest is a formal process that allows for public presentation of evidence relating to a death.
"The B.C. Coroners Service looks to gather the facts surrounding why a death took place. It is not a fault-finding agency."
Coroner's inquests are mandatory for any deaths that occur while a person was detained by - or in the custody of - a peace officer.
